findings: Built fresh QA fixtures (not reused from coder's tests) with shared[i32,?WG].

axc compile, no assignment (compile_file_kernel path, @strategy present, @workgroup(?WG,1,1) also holed): fails closed with CodegenError::UnresolvedStrategyHole (codegen-level backstop) -- never emits SPIR-V, never sizes an array from placeholder-1.

MCP compile_variant, no/empty assignments (compile_source_with_assignments_kernel path, which unconditionally strips @strategy text via F2 even with an empty map): fails closed with a HIR-level HirError::UndefinedStrategyHole (2 occurrences: @workgroup hole ref + shared-decl hole ref) -- again never reaches codegen, never emits placeholder-1 SPIR-V.

WITH assignment (axc compile --strategy-value WG=64 AND MCP compile_variant {"WG":64}): both compile successfully; disassembled the emitted SPIR-V (rspirv) and confirmed OpConstant %13 64 / OpTypeArray %4 %18 -- the shared array length is correctly 64 on BOTH entry points.

NUANCE (informational, not a defect): the literal CodegenError::UnresolvedSharedLenHole variant is NOT reachable via axc compile / MCP compile_variant / bench_variant on any input I could construct, because those entry points always hit an earlier backstop first (UnresolvedStrategyHole at codegen if @strategy survives with a still-holed @workgroup, or HirError::UndefinedStrategyHole at the driver's HIR-error gate if @strategy is textually stripped or the hole is undeclared). This is architecturally correct and matches the spec's own §1.3 explanation (the codegen backstop exists specifically to guard the axc-optimize enumerator's direct emit_module call, which bypasses the driver's HIR-error gate) -- I independently confirmed CodegenError::UnresolvedSharedLenHole DOES fire exactly as designed via AT-2976 (hand-built HIR, workgroup literal + no @strategy block) and AT-2983's negative arm (resolve_single_variant with a mismatched assignment name), both of which I re-ran in isolation and both PASS. Net effect for the user-facing guarantee ("never placeholder-1 silent miscompile"): verified true on every path I exercised, via one fail-closed mechanism or another.
